HOW TO WIN BOTS AND INFLUENCE PURCHASES
articles.summary: Shoppers are starting to let AI agents pick products and software for them. a16z and The Prompting Company report over 11,000 controlled agent tests to see how they choose. Stores with better return terms won 86% of equal-price comparisons in those tests. Agents also finished guest checkout forms most of the time, while every checkout requiring a new account stopped early. Mandatory signups stopped those agents, so keep guest checkout open and make return terms easy to compare.

articles.title: IS SAAS DEAD? THE 8 BUSINESS MODEL WAVES BEHIND THE DEBATE
articles.summary: One way to compete with a leader is to pick a problem people already pay to solve and ride a new wave that the leader would lose money copying. This is called counter-positioning. This post looks at the eight waves of counter-positioning that have appeared since 1994. It covers how monetized open source helped Red Hat become the first open-source company to reach $1 billion in yearly revenue, how Amazon's hourly rentals cut into Sun Microsystems' server sales, and much more.

articles.title: DOGFOODMAXXING
articles.summary: The best content shows how companies use their products themselves. This is probably the most convincing way to market a product. Show people how a team can use a product for a real job, and customers will see what they could do with it as well. If your team can't use your own product, use it for a dream customer and send them the result.

articles.title: THIS IS THE MOST IMPORTANT AEO AGENT YOU NEED TO BE RUNNING RIGHT NOW
articles.summary: AI search engines already cite outside websites when answering buying questions, giving outreach teams specific pages to approach. A marketing agency linked an AI agent to a spreadsheet and team inbox to find cited pages and contact their editors. The agency reports sending 206 emails and landing 28 live mentions in its initial client test, while tracked AI citations also climbed. Start with a small batch of pages and review every draft before enabling autonomous sending, since a human should still handle any payment or commercial terms.

articles.title: STOP ASKING USERS WHAT THEY WANT
articles.summary: Users will only tell you what they think they want. They don't know what they actually need because they haven't spent as much time thinking about it. Product engineers need to spend more time talking to users to understand their real problems so they can solve them. Ask questions that get real, useful intel on what to build.

articles.title: WATCHING USERS IS HOW YOU MAKE PRODUCTS BETTER
articles.summary: Few companies watch real people use their products anymore. Several people getting stuck in the same place marks a real problem, so repeat the sessions after a fix. Go where each person normally uses the product and let them use their own device. Give them a short script of basic tasks and ask them to think out loud while you say as little as possible.
